referents.why: 'to them' (autois), masculine plural, is the crowd that Pilate wanted to satisfy (cl1); ochlos is a singular collective, so the plural pronoun agrees in sense
'he delivered' (indicative) has Pilate as the agent of the release in cl0 and of the flogging and handing over
referents.category: subject carried across clauses of one agent

referents.why: 'He might be crucified' (subjunctive passive) has the flogged and handed-over Jesus as its implied subject (cl3, candidate w16); the builder pointed at the clause cl3s, not a person

links.why: the infinitive 'to satisfy the crowd' is the object of the participle 'wishing'
links.category: infinitive as object of a verb of wanting

links.why: the participle 'wishing' is the motive of the release in the finite clause
links.category: participle of motive within finite verb

links.why: the infinitive is nested inside the participle, which is inside cl0; a nested clause is not the next event after its container
links.category: sequence drawn from a nested clause

links.why: the participle 'having flogged' is the means of the handing over in cl3
links.category: participle of means within finite verb

links.why: hina with the subjunctive: Jesus was handed over in order that he might be crucified
links.category: purpose clause after a handing over

links.why: the Greek has no fused waw; the connective de sets the flogging against the release of Barabbas
links.category: sequence read where the text says but

links.why: the connective de (but) carried by cl3 sets Pilate's flogging of Jesus against his release of Barabbas in cl0 (mid-verse, backward link)
links.category: but between two acts of one agent
